cast.rowena: Acknowledges Rebecca’s care for Ivanhoe, offers help and asks whether she is leaving England.

rows.reason: The question at 61 is not yet an answer about destination; Granada is named at 62.
rows.openingParagraph:
“What means this, lady?” said the surprised bride; “or why do you offer
to me a deference so unusual?”
rows.closingParagraph:
“You leave England then?” said Rowena, scarce recovering the surprise
of this extraordinary visit.

rows.title: A departure intended

cast.rebecca: Says she and her father intend to leave for Granada and explains why she considers England unsafe for her people.
cast.rowena: Offers reassurance based on her husband’s and the king’s favour and Rebecca’s care for Ivanhoe.

rows.reason: The proposed journey is not a completed voyage. Retain the source’s Boabdil anachronism without silently correcting it.
rows.openingParagraph:
“I leave it, lady, ere this moon again changes. My father had a brother
high in favour with Mohammed Boabdil, King of Grenada—thither we go,
secure of peace and protection, for the payment of such ransom as the
Moslem exact from our people.”
rows.closingParagraph:
“But you, maiden,” said Rowena—“you surely can have nothing to fear.
She who nursed the sick-bed of Ivanhoe,” she continued, rising with
enthusiasm—“she can have nothing to fear in England, where Saxon and
Norman will contend who shall most do her honour.”

rows.title: The bridal veil

cast.rowena: Raises her veil at Rebecca’s request.
cast.rebecca: Asks to see Rowena unveiled and praises her beauty.

rows.reason: The gift has not yet been offered or opened.
rows.openingParagraph:
“Thy speech is fair, lady,” said Rebecca, “and thy purpose fairer; but
it may not be—there is a gulf betwixt us. Our breeding, our faith,
alike forbid either to pass over it. Farewell—yet, ere I go indulge me
one request. The bridal-veil hangs over thy face; deign to raise it,
and let me see the features of which fame speaks so highly.”
rows.closingParagraph:
“Lady,” she said, “the countenance you have deigned to show me will
long dwell in my remembrance. There reigns in it gentleness and
goodness; and if a tinge of the world’s pride or vanities may mix with
an expression so lovely, how should we chide that which is of earth for
bearing some colour of its original? Long, long will I remember your
features, and bless God that I leave my noble deliverer united with—”

rows.title: The farewell casket

cast.rowena: Receives Rebecca’s request to accept a casket.
cast.rebecca: Offers a casket in gratitude for Rowena’s husband’s help.

rows.reason: Contents and worked silver exterior are not disclosed until the next paragraph.
rows.openingParagraph:
She stopped short—her eyes filled with tears. She hastily wiped them,
and answered to the anxious enquiries of Rowena—“I am well, lady—well.
But my heart swells when I think of Torquilstone and the lists of
Templestowe.—Farewell. One, the most trifling part of my duty, remains
undischarged. Accept this casket—startle not at its contents.”
rows.closingParagraph:
She stopped short—her eyes filled with tears. She hastily wiped them,
and answered to the anxious enquiries of Rowena—“I am well, lady—well.
But my heart swells when I think of Torquilstone and the lists of
Templestowe.—Farewell. One, the most trifling part of my duty, remains
undischarged. Accept this casket—startle not at its contents.”

rows.title: The casket opened

cast.rowena: Opens the silver-chased casket and protests that she cannot accept its costly contents.
cast.rebecca: Urges Rowena to keep the diamond necklace and earrings and says she will wear jewels no more.

rows.reason: Rowena tenders the gift back, but Rebecca urges her to keep it. Acceptance is implied by the completed farewell, not a separately shown spoken agreement.
rows.openingParagraph:
Rowena opened the small silver-chased casket, and perceived a carcanet,
or neck lace, with ear-jewels, of diamonds, which were obviously of
immense value.
rows.closingParagraph:
“Yet keep it, lady,” returned Rebecca.—“You have power, rank, command,
influence; we have wealth, the source both of our strength and
weakness; the value of these toys, ten times multiplied, would not
influence half so much as your slightest wish. To you, therefore, the
gift is of little value,—and to me, what I part with is of much less.
Let me not think you deem so wretchedly ill of my nation as your
commons believe. Think ye that I prize these sparkling fragments of
stone above my liberty? or that my father values them in comparison to
the honour of his only child? Accept them, lady—to me they are
valueless. I will never wear jewels more.”

rows.title: A life of service chosen

cast.rowena: Offers companionship on conversion.
cast.rebecca: Refuses to change her faith and describes her intended charitable life before leaving.

rows.reason: No conversion or entry to a convent. Her plan to tend the sick is not a catalogue of already completed future deeds.
rows.openingParagraph:
“You are then unhappy!” said Rowena, struck with the manner in which
Rebecca uttered the last words. “O, remain with us—the counsel of holy
men will wean you from your erring law, and I will be a sister to you.”
rows.closingParagraph:
“Farewell,” she said. “May He, who made both Jew and Christian, shower
down on you his choicest blessings! The bark that waits us hence will
be under weigh ere we can reach the port.”

rows.title: The narrator’s close
rows.reason: Retrospective report of Rowena’s account to Ivanhoe, their later life and Richard’s death at Chaluz. No invented location for the couple’s conversation or physically present final battle cast.
rows.openingParagraph:
She glided from the apartment, leaving Rowena surprised as if a vision
had passed before her. The fair Saxon related the singular conference
to her husband, on whose mind it made a deep impression. He lived long
and happily with Rowena, for they were attached to each other by the
bonds of early affection, and they loved each other the more, from the
recollection of the obstacles which had impeded their union. Yet it
would be enquiring too curiously to ask, whether the recollection of
Rebecca’s beauty and magnanimity did not recur to his mind more
frequently than the fair descendant of Alfred might altogether have
approved.
rows.closingParagraph:
His fate was destined to a foreign strand,
A petty fortress and an “humble” hand;
He left the name at which the world grew pale,
To point a moral, or adorn a TALE.
